entries.name: Employer May Replace You
entries.summary:
Your employer, master, patron, household, supervisor, or client has alternatives and has made it clear that your position is not guaranteed.

Narrative effects: Job insecurity has taught you both to demonstrate your value and maintain consistent performance when replacement is possible.

entries.name: Everyone Else Moved On
entries.summary:
Friends, siblings, rivals, classmates, coworkers, or peers seem to have found careers, partners, homes, status, travel, or direction while you still feel as though your own life is waiting to begin.

Narrative effects: Comparison has made you sensitive to the different pressures shaping other people's choices and to the difference between appearances and actual satisfaction.

entries.name: Expected to Take Over the Business
entries.summary:
A shop, workshop, farm, inn, vessel, practice, office, caravan, or other business is expected to become your responsibility whether or not that was originally your plan.

Narrative effects: Succession pressure has made commercial decisions and responsibility for other people's work increasingly important.

entries.name: Failed Noble Suitor
entries.summary:
You pursued a courtship, marriage, patronage-linked relationship, or formal match involving noble or high-status expectations and failed to secure it.

Narrative effects: The failed pursuit taught you both the rules of formal courtship and how difficult it can be to persuade people whose decisions are constrained by status.

entries.name: Failed Your First Adult Responsibility
entries.summary:
One of the first responsibilities that was unquestionably yours ended badly. Someone depended on you, something important was neglected, or a task you were expected to handle simply went wrong.

Narrative effects: Failure taught you that adulthood is often defined by consequences other people cannot absorb for you.

entries.name: Family Debt Bearer
entries.summary:
A debt attached to your household, family, estate, business, or inherited obligations has become your problem to manage.

Narrative effects: You have learned to negotiate inherited obligations while examining records closely enough to understand what is genuinely owed.

entries.name: Family Name Disgraced
entries.summary:
Your family, household, clan, or inherited name carries a damaged reputation because of scandal, failure, accusation, crime, politics, debt, or another public disgrace.

Narrative effects: You have become highly aware of what people believe about your name and practiced at arguing against assumptions you did not personally create.

entries.name: First Real Contract on the Line
entries.summary:
Your first contract important enough to affect your future reputation, income, business, or career depends on whether you can deliver what you promised.

Narrative effects: You have learned to examine formal obligations carefully and negotiate details because failure now carries consequences beyond one payment.

entries.name: First Time You Had to Kill
entries.summary:
As an adult, circumstances finally placed you in a situation where killing another person or dangerous creature became something you actually did rather than only imagined.

Narrative effects: Lethal action taught you how fear and self-control matter when consequences cannot be undone. This trait does not determine what weapon or method was used.

entries.name: Friend Needs Your Help
entries.summary:
A friend has a serious problem and has turned to you because they trust you, lack better options, or believe you can actually help.

Narrative effects: Supporting someone close to you has required understanding their needs while remaining dependable when the situation becomes inconvenient.

entries.name: Fugitive Under Alias
entries.summary:
You are living under another name or deliberately altered identity because being recognized could bring arrest, capture, coercion, retaliation, or another serious consequence.

Narrative effects: Maintaining another identity has made both your story and your outward presentation matters of practical survival.

entries.name: Gang Escapee
entries.summary:
You recently left a gang, criminal crew, or coercive criminal network that may not accept your departure as final.

Narrative effects: Leaving criminal life has made you difficult to track and highly familiar with the informal structures you are trying to avoid.

entries.name: Good at a Life You Hate
entries.summary:
You have become competent at work, duties, or a way of life that increasingly makes you unhappy. Leaving means giving up something you are actually good at.

Narrative effects: You know how to keep performing despite dissatisfaction and understand that changing direction can require more courage than enduring what already works.

entries.name: Expedition Scribe
entries.summary:
You recorded supplies, routes, discoveries, deaths, contracts, maps, relic descriptions, and dangerous mistakes for an expedition, caravan, noble survey, temple mission, or ruin team.

Narrative effects: You know the official record is often cleaner than what actually happened.

entries.name: Farm Laborer
entries.summary:
You worked fields, barns, animals, harvests, irrigation, fences, tools, and weather as a young adult.

Narrative effects: You respect weather because it never negotiates.

entries.name: Fresh Academy Graduate
entries.summary:
You recently completed academy study, formal magical education, tutor certification, temple schooling, or institutional instruction.

Narrative effects: You still think of magic in lessons, warnings, diagrams, and instructors' voices.

entries.name: General Repair Hand
entries.summary:
You became the person called for ordinary repairs: gates, hinges, carts, roofs, shutters, handles, tools, fences, furniture, sheds, harness fittings, and whatever else had broken badly enough to matter but not badly enough to require a master craftsperson.

Narrative effects: You look for the actual point of failure before deciding whether something needs replacing.

entries.name: Guild Contract Holder
entries.summary:
You hold an active or recently completed guild contract that people can recognize. It marks you as someone doing formal work for coin, reputation, or obligation. Guild clerks, merchants, guards, and rivals may care about the terms.

Narrative effects: You read fine print before accepting praise.

entries.name: Guild Journeyman
entries.summary:
You completed enough training to function as a young journeyman, licensed assistant, guild worker, or recognized professional under guild expectations.

Narrative effects: You ask who trained someone, who certifies them, and who profits from the rules.

entries.name: Fascinated by Magic
entries.summary:
Whenever magic appeared, you wanted to know how it worked. You watched demonstrations, asked questions, inspected harmless enchanted objects, collected rumors, or searched for whatever explanations adults would allow you to hear.

Narrative effects: Magical phenomena invite investigation rather than passive awe. This trait represents interest and knowledge, not possession of an Arcana.

entries.name: First Familiar Bond
entries.summary:
A pet, working animal, stray, unusual creature, or familiar household beast became one of your closest childhood companions. Learning its habits taught you that communication does not always require words.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable building trust with animals through patience and attention. This bond does not grant Beast Arcana or magical control.

entries.name: Fought Other Children's Battles
entries.summary:
You regularly stepped into fights that did not begin as yours. Perhaps a friend was smaller, a sibling was targeted, or you simply could not tolerate watching someone be cornered.

Narrative effects: You know how quickly informal groups form around conflict and are willing to take physical responsibility when others hesitate.

entries.name: Found a Strange Relic
entries.summary:
As a child, you found or briefly handled an object that seemed older, stranger, or more significant than ordinary household possessions. It may have been genuine, misunderstood, harmless, dangerous, or later taken away.

Narrative effects: Unusual old objects draw your attention, and you instinctively consider both their material qualities and possible historical significance.

entries.name: Garden Child
entries.summary:
Gardens, orchards, hedges, flowerbeds, herbs, insects, soil, pruning, watering, and the slow changes of growing things occupied much of your childhood attention.

Narrative effects: Plants and cultivated environments feel familiar, and you naturally examine leaves, soil, stems, texture, and physical condition.

entries.name: Estate Tenant Child
entries.summary:
You spent childhood among tenant households whose daily life was tied to land or property controlled by a larger estate. Rents, dues, harvests, permissions, favors, and local customs shaped the community.

Narrative effects: You understand that rural life often involves negotiation and custom between the people working land and the people claiming authority over it.

entries.name: Farmyard Child
entries.summary:
Barns, fences, troughs, chickens, goats, cattle, horses, feed, mud, tools, and the constant presence of working animals defined much of your childhood play.

Narrative effects: Farm animals and ordinary rural conditions feel familiar, even if you later chose a life far from agriculture.

entries.name: Ferry Child
entries.summary:
You spent childhood around a ferry crossing where people, livestock, carts, goods, and messages repeatedly moved across a river, lake, channel, or strait.

Narrative effects: Small-watercraft movement and repeated crossings feel ordinary and practical.

entries.name: Festival Circuit Child
entries.summary:
Your childhood followed fairs, festivals, markets, seasonal gatherings, competitions, celebrations, performances, and temporary commercial crowds from place to place.

Narrative effects: Crowds feel like both audiences and marketplaces, and you understand the value of attracting attention before asking for an exchange.

entries.name: Fishing Boat Child
entries.summary:
Small working boats, nets, oars, sails, fish, wet decks, cold mornings, and repeated trips onto local waters were ordinary parts of childhood.

Narrative effects: Small-boat work under oar and simple sail feels familiar, though childhood experience does not make you a professional fisher.

entries.name: Forest Wanderer
entries.summary:
Forests, woods, groves, trails, clearings, game paths, streams, and the spaces beyond maintained roads formed much of your childhood playground.

Narrative effects: Wooded environments feel readable rather than featureless, and you naturally orient yourself through terrain and natural landmarks.

entries.name: Garden Helper
entries.summary:
You regularly helped in gardens, orchards, herb plots, courtyards, kitchen gardens, or landscaped grounds by watering, carrying, weeding, gathering, or simply staying close to the work.

Narrative effects: Cultivated plants and their physical condition feel familiar, especially when examined directly through leaf, stem, soil, and texture.

entries.name: Gatehouse Child
entries.summary:
You spent childhood around a gatehouse, checkpoint, toll point, estate entrance, bridge gate, or guarded entry where strangers regularly had to explain why they wanted through.

Narrative effects: You pay attention to arrivals and are comfortable with the social exchange involved in questioning, directing, or explaining access.

entries.name: Graveyard Keeper's Child
entries.summary:
Graveyards, burial grounds, memorial stones, funeral paths, mourning families, old names, and the practical work of maintaining places for the dead were familiar parts of childhood.

Narrative effects: Burial customs and old memorials feel familiar, and you naturally read graveyards as records of both faith and local history.

entries.name: Evasive Fighter
entries.summary:
You specialize in surviving attacks through movement rather than meeting every blow directly. Your training emphasizes slips, sidesteps, rolls, changes of angle, distance management, and reading the moment an opponent commits to an attack.

Narrative effects: You leave yourself routes to move and instinctively watch hips, shoulders, weapon lines, and footing for the instant an attack becomes difficult to redirect.

entries.name: Formation Fighter
entries.summary:
You specialize in fighting as part of an organized group rather than as an isolated duelist. You understand spacing, ranks, mutual protection, command calls, maintaining a line, controlled advances, and how individual movement affects everyone beside you.

Narrative effects: In a group fight you instinctively look for the line, the exposed flank, the person drifting out of position, and the space your allies need you to hold.

entries.name: Grappler
entries.summary:
You specialize in clinches, holds, throws, pins, locks, chokes, restraints, and controlling another person's body at close range. Your training focuses on leverage and position rather than simply exchanging strikes.

Narrative effects: You watch hips, shoulders, footing, weight distribution, and available leverage, always noticing when someone's position can be taken away from them.

entries.name: Enduring Intellect
entries.summary:
You combine endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain with memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Constitution and +4 Intelligence.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain and memory, structured reasoning, theory, and technical understanding together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Enduring Mobility
entries.summary:
You combine lasting endurance with fluid movement in nearly equal measure, staying coordinated even as effort accumulates. Grants +4 Constitution and +4 Dexterity.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain and agility, balance, speed, and bodily control together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Expressive Precision
entries.summary:
You combine aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement with presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Accuracy and +4 Communication.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement and presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Fine Coordination
entries.summary:
You combine agility, balance, speed, and bodily control with aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Dexterity and +4 Accuracy.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing agility, balance, speed, and bodily control and aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Focused Precision
entries.summary:
You combine aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement with resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Accuracy and +4 Willpower.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement and resolve, focus, emotional control, and resistance to pressure together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Forceful Combat
entries.summary:
Your aptitude strongly favors physical power, leverage, and force, while close-combat timing, pressure, defense, and weapon exchanges provides a meaningful secondary strength. Grants +6 Strength and +2 Fighting.

Narrative effects: You usually lead with physical power, leverage, and force, calling on close-combat timing, pressure, defense, and weapon exchanges to support that strength when the situation demands it.

entries.name: Forceful Precision
entries.summary:
You combine physical power, leverage, and force with aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Strength and +4 Accuracy.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing physical power, leverage, and force and aim, precision, hand control, and exact placement together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Forceful Presence
entries.summary:
You combine physical power, leverage, and force with presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Strength and +4 Communication.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing physical power, leverage, and force and presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Graceful Presence
entries.summary:
You combine agility, balance, speed, and bodily control with presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Dexterity and +4 Communication.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing agility, balance, speed, and bodily control and presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Grounded Presence
entries.summary:
You combine endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain with presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection in nearly equal measure. Grants +4 Constitution and +4 Communication.

Narrative effects: You tend to approach difficult situations by bringing endurance, resilience, recovery, and resistance to strain and presence, expression, persuasion, and social projection together rather than relying on either aptitude alone.

entries.name: Entertainer's Line
entries.summary:
Performers, musicians, actors, storytellers, dancers, festival workers, entertainers, or travelling artists recur through your family history. Audiences, applause, bad crowds, borrowed stages, reputation, and the need to hold attention became familiar long before you chose your own path.

Narrative effects: You notice audiences quickly and understand how timing, confidence, embarrassment, expectation, and attention can change a room.

entries.name: Fallen House
entries.summary:
Your family once possessed greater title, property, wealth, or influence than it holds today. You inherited the name, stories, expectations, and perhaps old relationships long after much of the power behind them disappeared.

Narrative effects: You recognize the difference between being treated with respect for what your family is and curiosity for what it used to be, and you pay close attention to how people react to a diminished but recognizable name.

entries.name: Family Under a Curse
entries.summary:
Your family believes, fears, or has credible reason to suspect that an inherited curse, supernatural debt, recurring omen, magical consequence, or pattern of unnatural misfortune follows the line. The exact cause and truth may be known, misunderstood, disputed, or still unresolved.

Narrative effects: You take recurring omens, inherited warnings, strange family patterns, and supernatural obligations more seriously than most. This trait does not define a new curse or reveal its truth by itself.

entries.name: Farmstead Line
entries.summary:
Generations of your family worked fields, animals, barns, orchards, fences, irrigation, harvests, or other rural livelihoods. Their inheritance is practical knowledge of land and livestock rather than courtly reputation.

Narrative effects: You notice weather, soil, animals, seasonal work, neglected maintenance, and whether someone understands where food actually comes from.

entries.name: Ferrykeeper Line
entries.summary:
Your family repeatedly operated ferries, crossing boats, river services, or other short-route transport where safe passage depended on reading current, loading people sensibly, and keeping a small vessel under control.

Narrative effects: You understand the practical work of repeated short crossings and the difference between simply being aboard a boat and actually controlling one.

entries.name: Firstblood House Scion
entries.summary:
You belong to one of the rare surviving Firstblood Houses, ancient dynasties whose recognized succession descends from the First Crowned. Your House may carry great hereditary dignity across modern borders, while ancient things tied to its lineage may sometimes recognize the blood and obligations you inherited.

Narrative effects: Your family belongs to a recognized Firstblood dynasty. This carries unusual pedigree and Ancestral Recognition, but does not grant universal authority, legal immunity, automatic magical power, or knowledge of ancient secrets.

entries.name: Fishing Family
entries.summary:
Generations of your family earned part or all of their living from rivers, lakes, coasts, nets, traps, small boats, or seasonal fisheries. The family memory is full of weather, catches, bad water, repaired gear, lean seasons, and the practical work of bringing food home from water.

Narrative effects: You understand the rhythms of working water and the natural conditions that shape when, where, and whether a catch is worth pursuing.

entries.name: Forester Family
entries.summary:
Foresters, woodsmen, coppice workers, charcoal burners, timber crews, woodland wardens, or other forest livelihoods recur through your family history. Trees were resources, boundaries, hazards, habitats, and long-term work rather than merely scenery.

Narrative effects: You understand managed woodland and the practical use, maintenance, and repair work that grows around timber-based livelihoods.

entries.name: Frontier Family
entries.summary:
Your family spent generations where settled authority, markets, healers, soldiers, or easy assistance could not be relied upon. Repairing, enduring, sharing work, preparing for shortages, and dealing with danger personally became part of the family's identity.

Narrative effects: You instinctively think about weather, distance, repair options, supplies, and the practical work required when outside help cannot be relied upon.

entries.name: Generations in Service
entries.summary:
Your family has spent generations as attendants, servants, stewards, retainers, household officers, estate workers, or trusted staff. Service is not shameful in your family memory; competence, discretion, reliability, and understanding how important households actually function are sources of pride.

Narrative effects: You notice who actually keeps a household functioning, what powerful people reveal around staff, and the difference between respectful service and degrading treatment.

entries.name: Gravekeeper Line
entries.summary:
Gravediggers, cemetery keepers, tomb attendants, burial workers, memorial caretakers, or people trusted with the dead recur through your family history. Burial customs, grieving families, old names, local memory, and respect for resting places were ordinary parts of the work.

Narrative effects: You are familiar with how faith and local custom shape burial, mourning, remembrance, and the treatment of the dead.

entries.name: Economic Scholar
entries.summary:
You study markets, trade networks, taxation, guild influence, supply, demand, credit, scarcity, commercial policy, and the movement of practical wealth through institutions and communities. Your expertise concerns economic systems rather than merely bargaining over one transaction.

Narrative effects: You read shortages, prices, cargo movement, guild behavior, debt, taxation, and control of resources as evidence of wider economic pressure.

entries.name: Engineer
entries.summary:
You understand structures, mechanisms, constructed systems, bridges, locks, lifts, gears, fortifications, tunnels, pressure systems, and the ways built things transmit force or fail. This is technical understanding rather than automatic mastery of every craft needed to build the design.

Narrative effects: You look for load paths, moving parts, tolerances, weak joints, hidden mechanisms, structural assumptions, and the component most likely to fail first.

entries.name: Faction Analyst
entries.summary:
You have developed substantial knowledge of organized power: noble blocs, guilds, temples, orders, armies, academies, rebel movements, cults, criminal networks, and other factions. You study their goals, resources, rivalries, internal fractures, public claims, and likely reactions without assuming personal membership in any of them.

Narrative effects: When an organization matters, you look for who leads it, who funds it, what it wants, where it is divided, and which relationships actually shape its choices.

entries.name: Folklorist
entries.summary:
You specialize in oral tradition, local legends, superstitions, songs, customs, household stories, cautionary tales, festival traditions, and the ways communities remember events outside formal archives. You know folklore can preserve truth, distortion, prejudice, metaphor, or all four at once.

Narrative effects: You compare local stories with older versions, cultural context, historical fragments, and the practical fears or values that may have shaped the tale.

entries.name: Forbidden Scholar
entries.summary:
You have studied knowledge that is banned, suppressed, dangerous, taboo, deliberately erased, or preserved only in restricted records. This may include prohibited magic, heresies, cursed practices, sealed entities, suppressed history, and other subjects that authorities or communities have reason to fear.

Narrative effects: You notice censored gaps, euphemisms, burned records, forbidden names, contradictory official accounts, and evidence that someone deliberately tried to prevent a subject from being understood.

entries.name: Geographer
entries.summary:
You study the physical organization of regions: terrain, rivers, coasts, mountain systems, climate zones, settlement patterns, natural barriers, and the spatial relationships that shape travel, trade, conflict, and habitation. Geography concerns the land itself more than the craft of drawing maps.

Narrative effects: You think in watersheds, passes, coastlines, climate, settlement patterns, and the physical relationships that explain why roads, borders, towns, and conflicts developed where they did.

entries.name: Earth Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Earth Arcana: stone, soil, weight, pressure, stability, and terrain. Your magic is grounded, defensive, forceful, and hard to move once set.

Narrative effects: You prefer steady footing and often judge places by their weight, walls, floors, and foundations.

entries.name: Enchantment Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Enchantment Arcana: wards, bindings, magical marks, persistent effects, conditional triggers, permissions, and enchanted objects.

Narrative effects: You instinctively notice magical bindings, marks, conditions, permissions, and the structure of persistent enchantments.

entries.name: Fiber Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Fiber Arcana: thread, cloth, rope, cordage, woven materials, knots, tension, and the structure of flexible fibers. Your magic favors precise manipulation, binding, reinforcement, repair, and control through material already present.

Narrative effects: You notice weave, tension, knots, fraying, stitching, and how cloth or cordage carries strain.

entries.name: Fire Arcana
entries.summary:
You have a natural gift for Fire Arcana: flame, heat, sparks, smoke, combustion, and explosive force. Your magic favors intensity, pressure, decisive action, and controlled destruction.

Narrative effects: Your emotions seem to warm the air around you, and your gaze lingers on flame longer than most people find comfortable.

entries.name: Eldmark Barrowland
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Eldmark's ancestral barrows, old claims, remembered kings, feud histories, inheritance customs, and formal respect for the past. Earth magic belongs to that same sense that land, stone, and memory outlast individual lives.

Narrative effects: You understand how old history and formal custom continue to shape present relationships. Earth Arcana reflects Eldmark's enduring cultural relationship with land and stone.

entries.name: Eldmark Beaconlander
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Eldmark's beacon towers, fortified routes, musters, remote holdings, and the practical duty of warning one settlement when danger threatens another. Earth magic fits a culture that relies on walls, roads, high ground, and the defensibility of familiar terrain.

Narrative effects: You recognize defensive geography, muster logic, beacon routes, and the practical movement between Eldmark communities. Earth Arcana is culturally familiar magic, not proof of military service.

entries.name: Eldmark Oathstone
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Eldmark's oath-stones, crown law, local assemblies, old promises, sacred places, and the belief that public commitments bind communities across generations. Earth magic reflects a culture rooted in land, stone, boundaries, barrows, and enduring places.

Narrative effects: You understand Eldmark's sacred and social weight of oaths, places, and communal obligation. Earth Arcana expresses the culture's connection to enduring land and stone without defining your faith or profession.

facts.label: Modifiers
facts.value: Earth Arcana +5, Religious Lore +8, Cultural Lore +8

entries.name: Emberhorn Accord-Bred
entries.summary:
You were shaped by the political Emberhorn of negotiated settlements, competing houses, written accords, public argument, and the difficult work of making strong interests coexist under law. Power magic mirrors that cultural ideal of strength brought under deliberate control.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable reading organized interests and arguing within systems where power must be negotiated rather than merely displayed. Power Arcana represents disciplined cultural magic.

entries.name: Emberhorn Housewise
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Emberhorn's established houses, written law, public obligation, family rank, cultured pride, and the expectation that power should be made legible through recognized forms. Power magic is a characteristic cultural expression of controlled strength rather than uncontrolled force.

Narrative effects: You understand Emberhorn house customs, formal conduct, and the responsibilities attached to recognized status. Power Arcana reflects a cultural tradition of disciplined magical force without reducing demon society to raw aggression.

entries.name: Emberhorn Steel-Law
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Emberhorn's martial institutions, disciplined public order, military obligations, and the belief that strength is respectable when controlled by law and responsibility. Power magic is part of that same cultural language of force made deliberate.

Narrative effects: You understand Emberhorn military discipline and the importance placed on controlling strength rather than indulging it. Power Arcana is a cultural magical foundation, not proof of military service.

entries.name: Fangbound Guest-Law
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Fangbound guest law, challenge customs, clan reputation, hospitality, negotiations between mobile groups, and the difference between authority that is claimed and authority others actually respect. Beast magic remains part of the culture's close relationship with living companions and herds.

Narrative effects: You understand Fangbound social obligations and how reputation shapes negotiation between clans and travelers. Beast Arcana is the culture's magical signature without defining your personal occupation.

entries.name: Fangbound Saddleborn
entries.summary:
You were shaped by the mounted side of Fangbound life, where herds, long travel, animal partnership, clan movement, and skill in the saddle are visible parts of status and survival. Beast magic is culturally familiar because animals are treated as active participants in life rather than distant resources.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable with mounts, working animals, and the practical relationships built around them. Beast Arcana reflects a Fangbound magical tradition and does not imply that every animal automatically obeys you.

entries.name: Fangbound Trailwise
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Fangbound hunting routes, seasonal movement, open-country travel, boundary signs, and the need to read what animals and people have recently done. Beast magic belongs naturally to a culture where understanding living creatures can matter as much as controlling them.

Narrative effects: You read trails and natural signs with confidence and understand how Fangbound communities move through shared territory. Beast Arcana is culturally learned magic rather than a profession.

entries.name: Freefang Bannerwise
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Freefang's mercenary banners, free companies, local protectors, shifting alliances, and settlements that often depend on whoever can actually keep an agreement. Motion magic suits a culture where mobility, rapid response, and the ability to relocate power matter constantly.

Narrative effects: You understand Freefang armed factions, protection arrangements, and the practical politics of forces that may serve one town today and another tomorrow. Motion Arcana reflects the culture's mobile character.

facts.label: Modifiers
facts.value: Motion Arcana +5, Faction Lore +8, Military Lore +8

entries.name: Freefang Fort-Town
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Freefang's hard-edged towns and fortified settlements, where reputation, local deals, capable protectors, and personal networks often matter more than distant law. Motion magic reflects a culture accustomed to changing circumstances and acting before opportunities disappear.

Narrative effects: You are practiced at learning who actually matters locally and persuading people whose authority may be informal. Motion Arcana represents Freefang's culturally mobile outlook.

entries.name: Freefang Roadfree
entries.summary:
You were shaped by Freefang roads, caravans, roadside bargains, moving work, independent travelers, and communities connected more by practical routes than central government. Motion magic is culturally useful wherever speed, travel, and getting from one opportunity to the next matter.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable with routes, changing terms, and the practical freedom created by movement. Motion Arcana is a cultural magical foundation rather than proof that you lived permanently on the road.

entries.name: Earth Arcana Mastery
entries.summary:
You have trained Earth Arcana beyond simple affinity into a major specialization. Your control is more precise, economical, and reliable inside its established domain, but mastery does not expand what the Arcana governs or remove mana costs, opposition, risk, or story consequences. This mastery grants the signature ability Stoneflow Passage.

Narrative effects: Treat Earth Arcana as a major specialization. Favor deliberate, technically informed expressions of the authored Earth Arcana domain; do not reinterpret it as another Arcana, grant effects outside its definition, or waive normal mana, strain, witnesses, and consequences. The character may use Stoneflow Passage when its fictional setup is plausible; it is a mastery technique, not automatic success or permission to exceed the Arcana domain.

entries.name: Earthwright
entries.summary:
You have deliberately learned to combine Earth Arcana and Engineering as one working discipline instead of treating them as unrelated skills. The overlap gives you options that depend on both kinds of competence and grants the signature ability Rapid Brace.

Narrative effects: Treat Earthwright as a genuine hybrid specialization. The character combines Earth Arcana with Engineering when both materially matter to the approach; do not let either skill substitute for the other or bypass normal tools, authority, resources, evidence, positioning, or consequences.

facts.label: Requirements
facts.value: characterLevel 10, Earth Arcana skill 30, Engineering skill 30, Earth Arcana trait 1

entries.name: Echo Arcana
entries.summary:
You carry a rare resonance with Echo Arcana, awakened through exposure, relic influence, violent history, lingering magic, or story consequence. Echo Arcana governs impressions left behind by events, voices, emotions, spells, wounds, deaths, and powerful presences. It does not simply reveal the past; it lets places, objects, and moments answer faintly after they should be silent.

Narrative effects: You notice repeated sounds, emotional residue, old violence, and places that still remember.

entries.name: Echo Arcana Mastery
entries.summary:
You have trained Echo Arcana beyond simple affinity into a major specialization. Your control is more precise, economical, and reliable inside its established domain, but mastery does not expand what the Arcana governs or remove mana costs, opposition, risk, or story consequences. This mastery grants the signature ability Echo Interrogation.

Narrative effects: Greyhaven knows you as one of its own, but some old silences around your arrival have never quite settled.

entries.name: Exposure Hardened
entries.summary:

Narrative effects: You notice exposure risks early and make small practical adjustments before discomfort becomes danger.

entries.name: Field Repairer
entries.summary:
