Narrative effects: You notice wear, weak joins, bad stitching, strained fittings, and small failures before they become expensive problems.

entries.name: Forceful Mover
entries.summary:
You specialize in applying bodily force to practical obstacles: forcing stuck doors, shifting debris, wrenching objects loose, dragging resistance, levering barriers, and overpowering stubborn mechanisms through direct physical effort.

Narrative effects: You look for where force can be applied most effectively before simply throwing your weight at an obstacle.

entries.name: Elder Care Helper
entries.summary:
You regularly assisted an elderly relative, neighbor, patient, or household member with meals, movement, medicine, company, or everyday tasks.

Narrative effects: You are sensitive to the needs of older people and familiar with basic care surrounding illness, weakness, or reduced mobility.

entries.name: Farmhand
entries.summary:
You were expected to help with real farm work: lifting, carrying, clearing, feeding, harvesting, digging, moving supplies, or whatever the season demanded.

Narrative effects: Physical agricultural work and the environmental conditions surrounding it feel familiar.

entries.name: Ferry Hand
entries.summary:
You work aboard a ferry or short-route passenger and cargo vessel, helping guide the craft, handle crossings, move passengers or goods, manage lines, and keep repeated trips running safely.

Narrative effects: You think of waterways in crossings, current, landing points, load balance, and how different the same route becomes when weather or traffic changes.

entries.name: Fishing Dock Helper
entries.summary:
You helped around working fishing boats by carrying gear, steadying craft, handling oars, assisting with simple sail work, and preparing vessels for departure or return.

Narrative effects: Small-boat propulsion and basic sail work are familiar through repeated dockside responsibility.

entries.name: Forest Path Runner
entries.summary:
You regularly carried messages, food, tools, or news along woodland paths between homes, camps, work sites, or nearby settlements.

Narrative effects: Moving quickly through wooded terrain feels familiar, and you pay attention to ordinary natural hazards along the route.

entries.name: Game Hall Scorekeeper
entries.summary:
You kept score, watched wagers, counted simple stakes, explained rules, fetched pieces, or helped maintain games in an inn, hall, festival, club, or household.

Narrative effects: Games of chance and stake-based play are familiar, along with the social behavior surrounding them. This trait does not imply addiction or criminality.

entries.name: Gang Lookout
entries.summary:
You were expected to watch streets, doors, alleys, rooftops, or approaches and warn older companions when guards, rivals, adults, or trouble appeared.

Narrative effects: You naturally choose useful sightlines and know how to watch an area without making your attention obvious.

entries.name: Graveyard Tender
entries.summary:
You helped clean paths, maintain markers, carry flowers, clear weeds, assist visitors, and perform simple work around a burial ground.

Narrative effects: Burial customs and the historical information preserved in memorials feel familiar.

entries.name: Escaped a Rising Flood
entries.summary:
Rising water trapped, separated, or threatened you while you were old enough to understand the danger and actively find a way through or around it.

Narrative effects: You learned to move through dangerous water and think about routes differently when ordinary roads, crossings, and landmarks become unusable.

entries.name: Failed First Casting
entries.summary:
Your first serious attempt at deliberate magic failed badly enough to become memorable. The spell collapsed, misfired, embarrassed you, frightened someone, or simply proved that wanting magic and controlling it were different things.

Narrative effects: Failure taught you to approach magical theory and personal control more seriously. This trait does not grant an Arcana.

entries.name: Failed Someone Who Trusted You
entries.summary:
Someone relied on you, and despite your intentions you failed them. The consequence may have been small or serious, but their disappointment stayed with you.

Narrative effects: You learned that good intentions do not erase consequences and became more conscious of the discipline reliability requires.

entries.name: Falsely Accused
entries.summary:
You were seriously accused of something you had not done and had to live with suspicion, defend yourself, or wait for the truth to emerge.

Narrative effects: You learned how difficult innocence can be to prove once a social group has accepted a convincing accusation.

entries.name: First Axe Lessons
entries.summary:
You were taught to fight with axes rather than merely use them as tools. The weight, edge alignment, recovery, and commitment behind each attack made a strong impression.

Narrative effects: Axes became your main early heavy one-handed attack style, with secondary familiarity using similarly forceful striking weapons.

entries.name: First Betrayal
entries.summary:
Someone you trusted knowingly betrayed that trust for advantage, fear, approval, convenience, or another reason you could not easily dismiss.

Narrative effects: You learned that understanding why someone acts does not mean trusting them, and you pay closer attention to relationships and motives.

entries.name: First Bow Lessons
entries.summary:
You received genuine instruction with a bow rather than merely playing at archery. Stance, draw, release, range, target focus, and safe handling became practiced skills.

Narrative effects: Archery became your primary early ranged foundation, with some familiarity carrying over to other aimed projectile weapons.

entries.name: First Brave Rescue
entries.summary:
You acted when another person or creature was in real danger, despite being frightened yourself. The rescue may have been small by adult standards, but the choice changed how you understood courage.

Narrative effects: You learned that courage is action under fear and that decisive behavior can cause others to follow.

entries.name: First Close-Quarters Lessons
entries.summary:
You were deliberately taught how to fight when opponents were close enough for grabs, shoves, knees, fists, and short weapons to matter.

Narrative effects: Unarmed fighting became your primary early combat foundation, supported by some familiarity with compact blades.

entries.name: First Crossbow Lessons
entries.summary:
You learned to load, handle, aim, and fire a crossbow under supervision. The mechanical nature of the weapon made the lessons different from ordinary archery, though both taught patience and ranged accuracy.

Narrative effects: Crossbows became your primary early ranged weapon, while broader projectile training gave you some familiarity with bows.

entries.name: First Greatblade Lessons
entries.summary:
You received supervised instruction with large swords or similarly heavy blades, usually using training weapons suited to your size. Reach, commitment, balance, and recovery mattered from the beginning.

Narrative effects: Large blades became your primary early weapon foundation, while basic blade principles also gave you some understanding of lighter swordplay.

entries.name: First Knife-Fighting Lessons
entries.summary:
Someone taught you how a knife or other light blade differs from simply waving a sharp object around. Close distance, quick attacks, free-hand movement, and fighting when space is limited became familiar concepts.

Narrative effects: You developed an early close-quarters fighting foundation combining light blades with unarmed movement.

entries.name: First Lance Lessons
entries.summary:
You were introduced to using a lance from horseback or through appropriate training exercises. Riding line, reach, commitment, and keeping the weapon controlled during movement were central to the lessons.

Narrative effects: Lance use became your primary early martial discipline, with secondary familiarity transferring to other thrusting pole weapons.

entries.name: First Long Journey
entries.summary:
You traveled far enough from home that landscapes, customs, accents, food, roads, or ways of living became noticeably different.

Narrative effects: Long-distance travel taught you both how routes connect and how quickly customs change between communities.

entries.name: First Mace-and-Club Lessons
entries.summary:
You learned that clubs, maces, hammers, and similar weapons depend on controlled impact rather than simply swinging as hard as possible.

Narrative effects: Bludgeoning weapons became your primary early fighting style, alongside modest familiarity with other weight-driven one-handed attacks.

entries.name: First Paid Work
entries.summary:
You completed work for actual payment rather than merely helping because family or adults expected it.

Narrative effects: Being paid taught you that labor has negotiable value and that effort, quality, and compensation do not always align automatically.

entries.name: First Polearm Lessons
entries.summary:
You received basic instruction with longer hafted weapons whose reach, leverage, and handling demanded more space and control than a simple spear or staff.

Narrative effects: Polearms became your primary early weapon foundation, supported by transferable staff handling.

entries.name: First Public Shame
entries.summary:
You were embarrassed, reprimanded, mocked, exposed, or humiliated in front of enough people that the memory changed how you thought about reputation.

Narrative effects: You became more aware of public expectations and how quickly embarrassment or reputation can spread through a group.

entries.name: First Real Grief
entries.summary:
You lost someone or something you genuinely loved deeply enough that grief became more than an abstract idea.

Narrative effects: Personal loss taught you something about how grief changes behavior and how people continue functioning while carrying it.

entries.name: First Sling Lessons
entries.summary:
You learned to use a sling properly, whether for sport, pest control, herding, hunting, or simple martial practice. Timing and controlled release mattered far more than the weapon's simplicity suggested.

Narrative effects: You developed an early foundation in sling use and a secondary familiarity with judging arcs and releases for thrown attacks.

entries.name: First Spear-and-Shield Lessons
entries.summary:
You learned basic spear fighting alongside shield use, practicing reach, thrusts, guarded movement, and keeping an opponent outside comfortable striking distance.

Narrative effects: You possess an early spear foundation supported by practical shield familiarity.

entries.name: First Spell Lessons
entries.summary:
You received your first structured lessons about deliberate spellcasting, mana control, magical safety, and the difference between theory and actual practice.

Narrative effects: Basic magical theory and the discipline surrounding spell practice became familiar, without automatically granting a specific Arcana.

entries.name: First Staff Lessons
entries.summary:
You were taught to use a staff as a weapon through controlled strikes, guards, changes of grip, reach, and movement rather than treating it as a simple stick.

Narrative effects: Staff fighting became your main early martial foundation, with some understanding of longer hafted weapons carrying over.

entries.name: First Storm at Sea
entries.summary:
You experienced a serious storm aboard a working vessel and saw how quickly ordinary sailing became urgent coordinated labor.

Narrative effects: Bad weather taught you practical respect for sail work and for hearing commands, warnings, and changes in a vessel through heavy noise.

entries.name: First Sword-and-Shield Lessons
entries.summary:
You received your first real instruction in fighting with a one-handed sword and shield. The lessons were basic, but they introduced distance, guard, footwork, attack, and active defense as parts of the same fighting style.

Narrative effects: You possess a genuine early foundation in one-handed weapon fighting supported by shield use, but not adult martial mastery.

entries.name: First Throwing Lessons
entries.summary:
You practiced deliberately throwing stones, darts, small javelins, knives, or other suitable objects at targets rather than relying on wild force.

Narrative effects: Thrown attacks became your primary early ranged skill, with some familiarity transferring to other release-based projectile weapons.

entries.name: First Thrown-Blade Lessons
entries.summary:
You practiced with knives or similarly balanced blades both in the hand and through deliberate throwing drills, learning that the two uses required different timing.

Narrative effects: Thrown weapons became your primary early skill, with practical familiarity handling light blades at close range.

entries.name: First Time Left Home Alone
entries.summary:
You made your first meaningful journey away from home without a parent or familiar adult supervising you directly.

Narrative effects: Independent travel taught you both how to find your way and how to ask unfamiliar people for useful information.

entries.name: Forbidden Book Discovered
entries.summary:
You discovered a book, record, manual, journal, or collection of writings that adults clearly considered dangerous, restricted, immoral, illegal, or better forgotten.

Narrative effects: Restricted knowledge became something concrete rather than abstract, and you learned how dangerous information can hide inside ordinary records.

entries.name: Found a Buried Charm
entries.summary:
You found a charm, token, relic, amulet, ward, or other deliberately hidden object beneath earth, floorboards, rubble, roots, or another concealed place.

Narrative effects: Unusual old objects make you consider both their historical significance and their physical authenticity or value.

entries.name: Found a Lost Child
entries.summary:
You encountered a younger or similarly aged child who had become separated from home, caregivers, or companions and helped work out where they belonged.

Narrative effects: You learned to combine practical searching with careful questions when helping someone who cannot clearly explain where they belong.

entries.name: Found an Old Map
entries.summary:
You discovered an old map, chart, property plan, route sketch, or geographic record that showed places differently from the world you knew.

Narrative effects: Old maps taught you that geography changes and that maps can preserve evidence of forgotten roads, borders, structures, and names.

entries.name: Got Lost Far From Home
entries.summary:
You became genuinely lost far enough from familiar surroundings that returning required observation, orientation, help, or luck.

Narrative effects: Being lost taught you to pay attention to direction, landmarks, and visible clues instead of simply continuing in panic.

entries.name: Enchanter
entries.summary:
You are professionally trained in the practical craft of preparing, stabilizing, modifying, and working with enchanted objects. This training includes a minimal functional awakening of Enchantment Arcana, enough to unlock the Arcana and participate in the craft without implying developed mastery or broad magical power.

Narrative effects: You examine materials, bindings, resonance, existing enchantment structure, and where magical influence is meant to settle before altering an enchanted object. Your Enchantment Arcana access is real but may still be rudimentary.

entries.name: Excavator
entries.summary:
You are experienced in digging, clearing rubble, opening blocked passages, recovering buried material, bracing unstable work, and judging how soil, stone, fill, timber supports, and confined spaces respond when disturbed.

Narrative effects: You think about load, collapse, spoil placement, bracing, leverage, access, and where displaced material must go before anyone starts digging enthusiastically.

entries.name: Expedition Planner
entries.summary:
You prepare dangerous or complicated journeys before departure by assessing personnel, supplies, tools, routes, weather, fallback plans, transport, communications, likely hazards, and mission priorities. Good expedition work reduces avoidable surprises without pretending risk can be eliminated.

Narrative effects: You ask what happens if the road closes, an animal is lost, food spoils, someone is injured, weather turns, a tool breaks, or the expedition has to return by a different route.

entries.name: Farmer
entries.summary:
You are professionally experienced in crop production and field work: soil preparation, planting, irrigation, weeding, harvest, storage, seasonal timing, tool use, and the practical effects of weather, pests, labor, and exhausted ground.

Narrative effects: You read fields by soil condition, growth, drainage, weeds, pest signs, tool marks, and whether the season's work is ahead of schedule or quietly failing.

entries.name: Ferryman
entries.summary:
You are practiced at operating ferries and small working vessels across rivers, channels, harbors, and difficult crossings. You understand current, landing approach, passenger balance, poles, oars, simple steering, loading, and the local judgment needed to make repeated crossings safely.

Narrative effects: You read current, wind, load balance, landing angle, boat response, and how much room a crossing really needs before pushing away from shore.

entries.name: Fisher
entries.summary:
You are professionally experienced at taking food and useful catch from rivers, lakes, coasts, or open water. You understand fish behavior, currents, seasons, bait, hooks, nets, cleaning, preservation, and the practical signs that tell you where a catch is likely to be.

Narrative effects: You read water by current, color, insects, birds, weather, depth, and small surface changes that tell an experienced fisher what is happening below.

entries.name: Forager
entries.summary:
You are professionally practiced at finding edible plants, water, fuel, useful roots, fungi, herbs, game signs, and other natural resources without exhausting the area or confusing a dangerous lookalike for something useful.

Narrative effects: You notice what can be safely gathered, where water is likely to collect, what has already been harvested, and which attractive plants or fungi should be left untouched.

entries.name: Gardener
entries.summary:
You are experienced in tending cultivated plants, herbs, flowers, kitchen plots, orchards, estate grounds, temple gardens, and other managed growing spaces. You understand soil, pruning, watering, pests, propagation, seasons, and the difference between a plant surviving and actually thriving.

Narrative effects: You notice thirsty leaves, bad pruning, compacted soil, pest damage, useful volunteers, and the quiet signs that a tended garden has been neglected or deliberately altered.

entries.name: Guild Professional
entries.summary:
You understand guild life from the inside: ranks, apprenticeships, journeymanship, charters, licenses, dues, workshop obligations, professional favors, trade protections, internal disputes, and the economics of organized skilled work.

Narrative effects: You ask who holds the charter, who trained whom, what work is protected, which dues are owed, and whether a claimed professional standing would actually be recognized.

entries.name: Elementborn — Ashborn
entries.summary:
Elementborn are mortal people whose ancestry carries a persistent elemental expression strong enough to shape physiology and magical affinity. Elementborn are not elementals, and their element does not determine culture, morality, profession, or personality. Ashborn carry smoke, ash, soot, haze, and volcanic-air traits such as charcoal undertones, smoke-like markings, darkened sclera, muted scent, or fine ash appearing around them under magical stress.

Narrative effects: Your body is unusually comfortable around smoke and airborne particulates and carries Smoke affinity. This does not grant immunity to suffocation, invisibility, or the ability to become smoke without explicit magic.

entries.name: Elementborn — Emberborn
entries.summary:
Elementborn are mortal people whose ancestry carries a persistent elemental expression strong enough to shape physiology and magical affinity. Elementborn are not elementals, and their element does not determine culture, morality, profession, or personality. Emberborn carry fire-linked traits such as unusual body heat, emberlike eyes, warm markings, soot-dark hair tones, or skin that handles heat unusually well.

Narrative effects: Your body and magic carry a stable Fire affinity. Heat-linked traits are inherited, but you do not automatically ignite objects, resist all fire, or possess fire abilities you have not learned.

entries.name: Elementborn — Frostborn
entries.summary:
Elementborn are mortal people whose ancestry carries a persistent elemental expression strong enough to shape physiology and magical affinity. Elementborn are not elementals, and their element does not determine culture, morality, profession, or personality. Frostborn carry cold-linked traits such as low body temperature, frostlike markings, pale or crystalline coloration, and exceptional comfort in severe cold.

Narrative effects: Your physiology is exceptionally adapted to temperature stress and carries Cold affinity. Cold skin and temperature sensitivity do not make you immune to freezing or harmful heat.

entries.name: Elementborn — Galeborn
entries.summary:
Elementborn are mortal people whose ancestry carries a persistent elemental expression strong enough to shape physiology and magical affinity. Elementborn are not elementals, and their element does not determine culture, morality, profession, or personality. Galeborn carry air-linked traits such as unusually light movement, hair or clothing that reacts readily to small currents, pale cloudlike markings, or an instinctive sense for changes in airflow.

Narrative effects: Your body favors light, controlled movement and carries Air affinity. This does not grant flight or immunity to falling without another established capability.

entries.name: Elementborn — Ironveined
entries.summary:
Elementborn are mortal people whose ancestry carries a persistent elemental expression strong enough to shape physiology and magical affinity. Elementborn are not elementals, and their element does not determine culture, morality, profession, or personality. Ironveined carry metal-linked traits such as metallic flecks in skin or eyes, unusual bodily density, mineral-colored nails, or heightened tactile awareness of worked metal and rigid materials.

Narrative effects: Your body carries a stable Metal affinity and unusually strong tactile response to dense materials. You are not literally made of metal and gain no automatic armor.

entries.name: Elementborn — Rootborn
entries.summary:
Elementborn are mortal people whose ancestry carries a persistent elemental expression strong enough to shape physiology and magical affinity. Elementborn are not elementals, and their element does not determine culture, morality, profession, or personality. Rootborn carry wood- and living-growth traits such as barklike patches, leaf or vine markings, earthy scents, unusual hair textures, or subtle seasonal changes in coloration.

Narrative effects: Your physiology carries Wood affinity and heightened organic scent awareness. You remain a mortal person rather than a plant creature and do not automatically photosynthesize, root, or regenerate.

entries.name: Elementborn — Stoneborn
entries.summary:
Elementborn are mortal people whose ancestry carries a persistent elemental expression strong enough to shape physiology and magical affinity. Elementborn are not elementals, and their element does not determine culture, morality, profession, or personality. Stoneborn carry earth-linked traits such as dense musculature, mineral flecks, stone-toned patches, heavy bones, or a grounded physical presence.

Narrative effects: Your body is unusually dense and carries an Earth affinity. This does not make you literally stone, immovable, or immune to ordinary injury.

entries.name: Elementborn — Stormborn
entries.summary:
Elementborn are mortal people whose ancestry carries a persistent elemental expression strong enough to shape physiology and magical affinity. Elementborn are not elementals, and their element does not determine culture, morality, profession, or personality. Stormborn carry lightning-linked traits such as static in the hair, bright irises, branching markings, tingling skin, or visible electrical reactions under stress.

Narrative effects: Your body and magic carry Lightning affinity and respond strongly to sudden exertion. You do not automatically discharge electricity or resist lightning without an explicit mechanic.

entries.name: Elementborn — Tideborn
entries.summary:
Elementborn are mortal people whose ancestry carries a persistent elemental expression strong enough to shape physiology and magical affinity. Elementborn are not elementals, and their element does not determine culture, morality, profession, or personality. Tideborn carry water-linked traits such as cool skin, subtle webbing, aquatic coloration, unusual comfort in water, or eyes resembling deep water.

Narrative effects: Your physiology is unusually comfortable in water and carries Water affinity. This does not grant underwater breathing unless another mechanic explicitly does so.

entries.name: Elf
entries.summary:
Elves are long-lived mortal humanoids with pointed ears, graceful proportions, and naturally keen senses. Their ancestry does not determine culture, profession, morality, magical tradition, or preference for nature; those come from Origin Culture, Upbringing, and lived experience.

Narrative effects: Your long-lived elven body carries sharp sight and hearing with naturally controlled movement. Do not infer archery training, animal affinity, Heroic Arcana, courtly behavior, or Lythael culture from Race alone.

entries.name: Foxfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Foxfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus fox ears, one or more foxlike tails, keen hearing, sharp eyes, and agile movement. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Sharp hearing, strong visual awareness, agile movement, and quiet footwork favor noticing danger and moving unobtrusively. Foxfolk ancestry does not imply deception, trickery, playfulness, or dishonesty.

entries.name: Gnome
entries.summary:
Gnomes are small mortal humanoids with fine hand control, sensitive touch, sharp close attention, and compact bodies suited to precise manipulation. Gnome ancestry does not automatically make someone an engineer, alchemist, scholar, inventor, or mage.

Narrative effects: Your hands and tactile perception are naturally precise, making small details and delicate manipulation easier to manage. Technical knowledge still comes from actual training.

entries.name: Goatfolk Beastkin
entries.summary:
Goatfolk Beastkin are kemonomimi-style beastkin with fully humanlike faces and bodies plus goat horns, goat ears, sturdy human feet or practical mountain footwear, and sure-footed movement. They are not animal-headed, muzzled, furry-bodied, paw-handed, digitigrade animal-bodied, or full anthropomorphic animals.

Narrative effects: Sure-footed balance and strong climbing instincts make steep slopes, broken ground, narrow ledges, and vertical movement unusually natural. Stubbornness is not an enforced personality trait.

entries.name: Empathic Listener
entries.summary:
You are skilled at understanding and emotionally reaching people through patience, careful questions, reassurance, and genuine attention. You can help people feel heard without forcing agreement, manufacturing trust, or overriding their choices.

Narrative effects: You give people enough room to reveal what they are feeling before deciding what might actually help.

entries.name: False Identity Specialist
entries.summary:
You are skilled at maintaining an invented social identity over extended interaction. You understand that a false name needs believable manners, status cues, habits, dress, explanations, and knowledge of how someone in that role is expected to behave.

Narrative effects: You build false identities from the small details that keep other people from asking the next dangerous question.

entries.name: Fine Ball Attire Set
entries.summary: Elegant formal clothing suited for dances, court gatherings, noble celebrations, and social occasions where appearance becomes a weapon.

entries.name: Frontier Travel Clothes Set
entries.summary: Hard-wearing clothes for dangerous roads, border settlements, rough camps, and places where help arrives late. Less refined than city travel wear, but more forgiving.

entries.name: Gambeson Set
entries.summary: A sturdy quilted gambeson meant to absorb impact, soften cuts, and serve either as light protection or padding beneath heavier armor. Practical, warm, and common among soldiers and travelers.

entries.name: Estoc
entries.summary: Starting weapon for Dueling. A stiff thrusting sword designed to find gaps in.

entries.name: Fauchard
entries.summary: A long polearm with a forward-curving blade suited for hooking, slashing, and controlling reach from outside sword range.

entries.name: Flail
entries.summary: A chain-linked striking weapon used to wrap around shields, punish guarded enemies, and deliver unpredictable impact. Dangerous to the wielder without training, and worse for the enemy with it.

entries.name: Glaive
entries.summary: Starting weapon for Polearms. A long pole blade suited for sweeping cuts and re.

entries.name: Great Axe
entries.summary: A heavy two-handed axe built for overwhelming force, shield-breaking swings, and terrifying execution blows. It is not subtle, but few things that survive it care about subtlety.

entries.name: Greatsword
entries.summary: A large two-handed sword built for reach, weight, and decisive cutting force. It is difficult to hide, exhausting to use poorly, and terrifying when carried by someone trained to let momentum speak.

entries.name: Escaped a Gang
entries.summary:
You left a gang, criminal crew, violent peer group, or similar organization that did not expect members to simply walk away.

Narrative effects: Leaving taught you the practical value of moving quickly, staying difficult to find, and avoiding familiar patterns.

entries.name: Evicted With the Household
entries.summary:
Your household lost the right or ability to remain where you lived, forcing everyone to relocate with limited control over the timing.

Narrative effects: Sudden relocation taught you to think practically about where to go next and what terms might secure another place to stay.

entries.name: Exiled Teen
entries.summary:
You were formally or effectively forced away from your home, community, institution, territory, or people while still a teenager.

Narrative effects: Exile exposed you to unfamiliar communities and made route-finding away from home a practical necessity.

entries.name: Expelled Without Scandal
entries.summary:
You were removed from a school, academy, guild program, monastery, military institution, or other structured path for comparatively ordinary reasons rather than spectacular wrongdoing.

Narrative effects: Institutional failure taught you about expectations, consequences, and continuing after a structured path closes. Do not invent a hidden scandal unless established elsewhere.

entries.name: Failed to Join the Guard
entries.summary:
You attempted to join a guard, militia, watch, military unit, or similar organization and were rejected or failed to qualify.

Narrative effects: Preparing for recruitment still taught you about military expectations and the discipline required to meet formal standards.

entries.name: First Duel Lost Badly
entries.summary:
Your first serious duel or formal fight ended decisively against you. Pain, humiliation, fear, or simple technical inferiority made the lesson impossible to ignore.

Narrative effects: Defeat still taught you real combat lessons and made returning to a serious fight an act of courage rather than ignorance.

entries.name: First Duel Won
entries.summary:
You won a serious duel, spar, challenge, or formal fight that mattered to the people watching and to your own sense of ability.

Narrative effects: Victory gave you confidence in formal combat and experience carrying yourself when others look to the winner.

entries.name: First Kill Remembered
entries.summary:
You killed a person or dangerous creature for the first time and found that the memory stayed with you long after the immediate danger passed.

Narrative effects: You understand that lethal action has consequences beyond the moment itself. This trait does not define which weapon or method was used.

entries.name: First Love Scandal
entries.summary:
Your first serious romantic attachment became the subject of gossip, disapproval, embarrassment, exposure, or conflict.

Narrative effects: You learned how private feelings can become difficult to conceal and how exposure affects everyone involved.

entries.name: First Spell Gone Wrong
entries.summary:
A serious attempt at magic failed badly enough to become a defining teenage memory. The spell collapsed, misfired, caused damage, frightened someone, or exposed how much control you still lacked.

Narrative effects: You learned to treat magical failure as something to understand and control rather than simply fear. This trait does not grant a specific Arcana.

entries.name: First Spell Saved Someone
entries.summary:
Magic you used, helped direct, or understood made a real difference when someone was in danger. The experience proved that magical knowledge could matter under pressure.

Narrative effects: You associate magic with decisive action under pressure. This trait does not establish Healing Arcana or any other specific form of magic.

entries.name: Forbidden Romance
entries.summary:
A romantic relationship was forbidden or strongly opposed because of family, status, culture, faction, faith, politics, law, or another external boundary.

Narrative effects: You learned to balance another person's feelings against the practical need for secrecy. This trait does not establish the relationship as still active.

entries.name: Friendship Became Rivalry
entries.summary:
A close friendship became competitive, strained, resentful, or openly rivalrous as your ambitions, relationships, abilities, or circumstances changed.

Narrative effects: Competition taught you to control yourself while remaining conscious of the personal feelings beneath rivalry.

entries.name: Early Magic Prodigy
entries.summary:
You displayed exceptional natural magical aptitude during your teenage years. Magic came to you with unusual speed and intuition, and teachers or other experienced practitioners recognized that your potential was far beyond what they normally expected from someone your age. Your talent applied to the forms of magic you genuinely possessed rather than granting mastery over every Arcana.

Narrative effects: The character was genuinely regarded as a magical prodigy during adolescence. Their unusual gift concerns the Arcana and magical capabilities they actually possess; it never grants an Arcana, spell, or ability by itself. Their rapid progress and exceptional magical aptitude are established parts of their history rather than merely academic knowledge.

entries.name: Estate Worker
entries.summary:
You worked across the practical needs of a larger estate: fields, grounds, repairs, harvests, fencing, stores, animals, roads, or whatever work needed another capable pair of hands.

Narrative effects: Estate work gave you broad environmental familiarity and practical competence maintaining ordinary physical things.

entries.name: Failed Academy Student
entries.summary:
You spent meaningful time in formal education but failed to complete the path successfully. Poor results, missed expectations, personal difficulties, changing circumstances, or simply not fitting the institution eventually ended your studies.

Narrative effects: Failure did not erase what you learned. You retain substantial experience with formal study and the discipline required to work through difficult material.

entries.name: Farmstead Worker
entries.summary:
You spent your teenage years doing sustained agricultural work: planting, harvesting, repairing, moving supplies, handling seasonal tasks, and performing physically demanding jobs around a farmstead.

Narrative effects: Years of agricultural work gave you substantial environmental familiarity and practical physical strength.

entries.name: Fisher's Apprentice
entries.summary:
You trained aboard small fishing vessels or around working fisheries, learning oars, simple sails, gear, departure routines, and the physical demands of getting a catch home.

Narrative effects: Small-vessel propulsion under oar became a major skill, supported by practical sail experience.

entries.name: Forbidden Text Reader
entries.summary:
Your teenage studies repeatedly led you toward writings that were restricted, censored, dangerous, immoral, illegal, or deliberately hidden from ordinary students.

Narrative effects: You became practiced at locating and understanding restricted knowledge while learning that written information can carry real consequences.

entries.name: Gang Runner
entries.summary:
A gang or criminal crew used you for messages, collections, introductions, distractions, lookout work, or other low-level tasks during adolescence.

Narrative effects: You learned how criminal groups communicate, recruit, conceal their business, and maintain believable explanations.

entries.name: Guild Apprentice
entries.summary:
You entered a guild-controlled apprenticeship or training program where practical work came with rules, hierarchy, traditions, dues, expectations, and a recognized professional community.

Narrative effects: You gained broad craft competence while learning the customs and expectations of organized professional life.

entries.name: Fostered Between Homes
entries.summary:
You spent your first years moving between two or more established homes under a fostering, custody, kinship, protection, or practical arrangement. Each place had its own rules and expectations.

Narrative effects: You learned early that what counts as proper behavior depends heavily on which household door you have just walked through.

entries.name: Found After Vanishing
entries.summary:
You disappeared once as a toddler and were later found somewhere strange, dangerous, impossible, or embarrassingly close by. Adults remembered the fear of searching for you.

Narrative effects: People losing track of you feels familiar rather than frightening.

entries.name: Found in the Rain
entries.summary:
You were found during rain, storm, mud, or miserable weather, too young to explain how you survived. Some call it luck, some call it mercy, and some still wonder who left you there.

Narrative effects: Rain makes you quiet, as if some part of you still remembers being discovered under it.

entries.name: Early Questioner
entries.summary:
Once you learned to ask questions, you did so relentlessly. Who, why, where, what, and how became tools for testing every adult's patience.

Narrative effects: Asking people directly for explanations still feels more natural than quietly remaining confused.

entries.name: Early Walker
entries.summary:
You were on your feet earlier than expected and quickly became difficult to keep in one place. Once movement became possible, you used it constantly.

Narrative effects: Movement feels more natural to you than standing around waiting for something to happen.

entries.name: Fascinated by Firelight
entries.summary:
Candles, hearths, lanterns, sparks, and dancing flame could hold your attention far longer than adults expected. Where some children recoiled, you watched.

Narrative effects: Flame draws your attention without immediately frightening you. This temperament does not imply Fire Arcana.

entries.name: Feared Deep Water
entries.summary:
Water you could not stand comfortably in frightened you. Wells, deep pools, rivers, docks, and boats could provoke an instinctive need to stay close to safety.

Narrative effects: You respect deep water and have learned to function despite the fear it once provoked.

entries.name: Feared Dogs
entries.summary:
Barking, teeth, fast movement, or simply unfamiliar dogs frightened you as a toddler. Even friendly animals could trigger immediate caution.

Narrative effects: You pay close attention to canine behavior and know the difference between controlling fear and pretending an animal cannot hurt you.

entries.name: Fed Every Animal
entries.summary:
Pets, livestock, birds, strays, and any creature willing to approach you were likely to receive pieces of your food whether adults approved or not.

Narrative effects: You pay attention to what animals want and how they react when approached.

entries.name: Followed Music
entries.summary:
A song somewhere nearby could pull you across a room, down a hall, or toward an open window. You wanted to know where music was coming from.

Narrative effects: Melody, rhythm, and unusual musical sounds catch your attention quickly.

entries.name: Followed Older Children
entries.summary:
Older siblings, cousins, wards, or neighborhood children seemed far more interesting than adults. You followed them, copied them, and tried to understand their games and rules.

Narrative effects: You are good at observing a group's informal rules and figuring out how people fit together socially.

entries.name: Gentle With Small Things
entries.summary:
Insects, tiny animals, fragile objects, flowers, small toys, and anything easily damaged brought out unusual care in your hands.

Narrative effects: You instinctively moderate your touch around delicate things and vulnerable living creatures.

entries.name: Endurance Conditioning
entries.summary:
Years of deliberate conditioning, long marches, hard drills, or sustained physical work trained your body to keep functioning as fatigue accumulates. Grants +2 Constitution and +1 Strength.

Narrative effects: You pace effort instinctively, conserve energy when possible, and recognize the difference between discomfort and genuine physical failure.

entries.name: Explosive Power Drills
entries.summary:
You trained short bursts of force through jumps, sprints, launches, rapid lifts, and other movements that demand power immediately rather than over time. Grants +2 Strength and +1 Dexterity.

Narrative effects: You coil before sudden effort and instinctively coordinate legs, hips, and timing when a task demands immediate power.

entries.name: Fear Conditioning
entries.summary:
You deliberately practiced functioning while afraid through controlled exposure, dangerous training, harsh drills, or repeated work where panic would make matters worse. Grants +2 Willpower and +1 Constitution.

Narrative effects: Fear still registers, but you are practiced at separating the body's alarm response from the decision about what you actually do next.

entries.name: Formation Combat Drills
entries.summary:
You trained to fight as part of an organized line, maintaining spacing, weapon lanes, mutual protection, and awareness of orders around you. Grants +2 Fighting and +1 Intelligence.

Narrative effects: You think about adjacent allies, lanes of movement, exposed flanks, and whether your position helps or endangers the people fighting beside you.

facts.label: Modifiers
facts.value: Polearms +8, Shields +5, Military Lore +3, Fighting +2, Intelligence +1

entries.name: Grappling Practice
entries.summary:
You practiced holds, escapes, leverage, clinches, takedowns, and contests of bodily control. The discipline turns strength into close-range technique rather than simple force. Grants +2 Strength and +1 Fighting.

Narrative effects: At close range you naturally notice balance, grip, hips, shoulders, and where an opponent can be turned or pinned.

entries.name: Elven Enclave
entries.summary:
You were raised in an elven-majority enclave, estate, town, or community whose own history, manners, institutions, art, and social expectations shaped everyday life. You need not be an elf yourself.

Narrative effects: You are familiar with an established community's history and formal social habits without assuming all elves share one personality or way of life.

entries.name: Estate Tenant Village
entries.summary:
You grew up among households farming, herding, or working land controlled by a larger estate. Rural work mixed with rents, dues, customary rights, estate authority, shared obligations, and local traditions.

Narrative effects: You understand both rural environmental knowledge and the customs and social arrangements through which tenant communities organize daily life.

entries.name: Farm Household
entries.summary:
You were raised in a working farm household where crops, livestock, weather, planting, harvest, fencing, feed, births, repairs, and seasonal labor structured the year.

Narrative effects: You possess everyday familiarity with working animals and the environmental conditions that determine whether rural work succeeds.

entries.name: Ferry Settlement
entries.summary:
You grew up where moving people, animals, carts, and goods across a river, strait, lake, or other crossing formed an important part of local life.

Narrative effects: Repeated crossings made small-watercraft propulsion and control familiar parts of ordinary life.

entries.name: Festival Caravan
entries.summary:
You grew up among vendors, performers, cooks, craftsmen, animal handlers, laborers, games, temporary stalls, fairs, seasonal gatherings, and the constant need to attract a crowd before moving onward.

Narrative effects: You are comfortable gaining public attention and negotiating everyday exchanges in temporary, competitive marketplaces.

entries.name: Fishing Fleet Household
entries.summary:
You were raised among working fishers whose household followed boats, nets, catches, weather, markets, tides, repairs, and the daily uncertainty of returning with enough.

Narrative effects: You are familiar with practical small-vessel work under sail and sustained use of oars.

entries.name: Frontier Homestead
entries.summary:
You were raised on the edge of settled lands where households repaired their own property, understood the surrounding terrain, preserved supplies, and solved practical problems before distant specialists could arrive.

Narrative effects: You are familiar with practical repair and the plants, animals, weather, terrain, and hazards surrounding isolated settlement.

entries.name: Garrison Town
entries.summary:
You grew up in a civilian settlement whose economy, politics, streets, businesses, and public life were heavily shaped by a permanent military presence. Soldiers were common without necessarily being members of your household.

Narrative effects: You understand the place of military institutions within local society and how organized groups compete for authority, resources, and influence.

entries.name: Guildhall Raised
entries.summary:
You spent formative years around a guildhall, trade association, professional fraternity, or organized body of craftspeople and merchants. Masters, apprentices, contracts, standards, disputes, dues, reputations, and professional politics were familiar.

Narrative effects: You understand how organized professional groups function and are accustomed to the standards by which goods and workmanship are judged.
